newsitem.title: CANADA: Repap shrs slump on takeover deal doubts.
newsitem.headline: Repap shrs slump on takeover deal doubts.

text.p: Shares of Repap Enterprises Inc slumped on Wednesday on growing doubts that a proposed takeover by Avenor Inc would proceed as planned, analysts said.
Repap shares were off 0.50 to 2.87 on volume of more than 3.3 million shares in late trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange. Repap topped Toronto actives.

Analysts said Repap shareholders appeared unconvinced that Avenor's planned C$3 billion takeover of the pulp and paper company would get the necessary two-thirds vote from Avenor shareholders on February 28.
"The market is saying that it doesn't like this deal," said an analyst who declined to be identified.

Analysts said Avenor investors appeared concerned about the C$2.5 billion of Repap debt that Avenor would assume with the all-stock merger. On Tuesday, Avenor shares fell 0.75 to 21.20 on turnover of 112,000 shares.

Repap shareholders must also approve the merger by a two-thirds vote. Failure to get shareholder approval would scuttle the merger, forcing Repap to find another solution to its growing financial troubles.
Aside from Avenor, no other large forest products company appeared ready to make an offer for the entire company.
"I don't know of any other suitors waiting in the wings," said the analyst.
That could force Repap's creditors, which included Toronto-Dominion Bank, to agree to ease the company's considerable debt costs.
Repap might also need to consider selling one or more of its pulp and paper facilities, which are in New Brunswick, Manitoba, British Columbia and Wisconsin.
Analysts said they eagerly awaited information circulars on the proposed merger. The circulars were expected to be available later in January and would contain further details on the transaction.
